content.title: Easter supermarket times: When are Lidl, Aldi and Dunnes open?
content.text: Households around the country are currently celebrating Easter Sunday, holding out hope that they don’t run out of chocolate eggs. If they do, however, there will be a limited amount of time to rush to the shops and restock their baskets. Aldi won’t be an option on Easter Sunday, though, as the retailer has closed all 166 branches for the holiday. Aldi has closed all 166 branches for the holiday. Pic: ChameleonsEye/Shutterstock The supermarket will be back open for the bank holiday on Easter Monday, working on reduced hours. On Monday. Aldi will be opening one hour later than usual at 9am and closing one hour earlier at 9pm. Similarly, Dunnes Stores has closed all 138 of its Irish branches for Easter Sunday. Dunnes Stores has also closed all 138 of its Irish branches. Pic: Artur Widak/NurPhoto/REX/Shutterstock Before resuming normal operations from Tuesday, most shops are expected to be open from 9am to 7pm on the bank holiday. However, each branch will have its own arrangement and customers are urged to check the individual shop’s times. Meanwhile, Supervalu will be maintaining its typical Sunday schedule on both Easter Sunday and Monday. Supervalu will be maintaining its typical Sunday schedule. Pic: Colin Keegan/Collins Dublin Like Dunnes, individual branches will have their own plans. For Tesco, selected branches are shut for Easter Sunday, while others will run bank holiday hours. The outlets will typically work from 9am to 8pm on the bank holiday, though some branches may also differ. Lidl supermarkets are open for reduced hours of 9am to 6pm. Pic: Lidl Ireland Finally, Lidl supermarkets are open for reduced hours of 9am to 6pm on Easter Sunday. The branches will then be open from 9am to 9pm on Monday before resuming normal opening hours the following day. In the meantime, Easter Sunday has marked the first celebration with Pope Leo XIV at the helm. The holiday comes almost a year after the death of Pope Francis, who was last seen on Easter Sunday 2025. Taking to social media this weekend, Pope Leo spoke of the ‘severing of bonds through war.’ He said: ‘Even today there are tombs to be opened, and often the stones sealing them as so heavy and so closely guarded that they seem to be immovable. ‘Some weigh heavily on the human heart, such as mistrust, fear, selfishness and resentment; others, stemming from these inner struggles, sever the bonds between us through war, injustice and the isolation of peoples and nations.’ Listen to our Podcasts Share Now
